title: CT model distinguishes recorded psychiatric diagnosis groups
summary: A DenseNet-based multiple-instance model classified CT scans from patients with bipolar disorder or schizophrenia and healthy controls. Development used 685 people, with another 105 from two additional centers for testing; the paper reports 72.4% external accuracy. Cases and healthy controls came from different hospitals, so acquisition or site differences may contribute to classification. The retrospective result does not establish a diagnostic brain mechanism, screening benefit or performance beyond these selected groups.
organization: Shandong University; Shandong First Medical University

source_review.scope: Primary relevant recruitment/reference, patient partition, DenseMD model Methods, Table1–3 and primary Fig2, Results and limitations; supplementary scanner table not inspected. Exact primary identity/date and fresh primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: Retrospective three-group classification against DSM-V-based clinical diagnoses and healthy-control assessments. Training/validation used 506 psychiatric patients and 179 controls; external testing used 65 patients and 40 controls, with Table2 accuracy .724. Primary Fig2 explicitly shows Normal, Bipolar and Schizo outputs, resolving an inconsistent binary-task phrase in the Results.
evidence.unknown: Performance independent of hospital/scanner confounding, medication effects and selection bias remains unestablished. Patients and controls were sourced from different centers in both development and testing. No screening effectiveness or patient benefit was tested.
evidence.ai_role: A shared three-dimensional DenseNet encoder learns representations from eight brain-CT patches per person, fuses them and classifies recorded clinical groups through multiple-instance learning.
